system.name: PCS
system.one_liner: a generic scheduling framework that meets operator-specified objectives by tuning Weighted-Fair-Queuing policies

components.name: Operator
components.role: specifies high level objectives via the preference framework

components.name: Preference Solver
components.role: uses a simulation-based search strategy to find Pareto-optimal WFQ configurations

components.name: User
components.role: submits jobs with a demand function on the critical path

components.name: Resources
components.role: WFQ queues (weighted by w1/w2/w3) that process user jobs according to the chosen policy

content.key_idea: PCS separates a slow control loop, where operators tune scheduling preferences via a simulation-based solver, from the fast critical path, where user jobs are scheduled through tuned Weighted-Fair-Queuing resource queues.
content.reading_order: Top band, left to right: operator exchanges preference metrics with the interface and solver (steps 1-4); bottom band: user jobs flow through the resulting WFQ queues to resources.

summary: This figure gives an overview of PCS, a generic cluster scheduling framework built around Weighted-Fair-Queuing (WFQ). The diagram is split by a dashed horizontal line into two tiers. In the top control-loop tier, an Operator exchanges average prediction-error and JCT metrics with a Preference Interface (step 1), which invokes a simulation-based Preference Solver running many simulations (step 2) that returns Pareto-optimal WFQ configurations for the operator to select from (step 3); the resulting policy is then pushed down to configure the Resources (step 4). In the bottom critical-path tier, a User submits a job and its demand function directly to the WFQ-organized Resources, which are partitioned into three weighted queues (w1, w2, w3) by job-size thresholds t1 and t2, and returns a predicted job completion time (JCTpred). Red arrows mark the solver invocation and the user's live request/response, while black arrows carry the more static preference and policy exchange.
